title: Priority claim: the 3 x n holed-strip knight graph with two far corners removed - open and closed tour existence characterisation, Lean 4 formalized (AI4Math pipeline)
description: Priority claim of record (not a full paper). Contents: the claim note (LaTeX source + PDF), the Lean 4 sources (Lean v4.34.0, mathlib4 v4.34.0 rev 5ed29652; 0 sorry; #print axioms whitelist-checked) and the audit and novelty-search evidence. Result: for the knight graph K_n of the 3 x n chessboard with the two far corners (0,0) and (2,n-1) removed, the exact existence characterisation of tours is proved in Lean 4 - an open tour (Hamiltonian path) exists if and only if n is 1, 4, 5, or at least 8, and a closed tour (Hamiltonian cycle) exists if and only if n is even and at least 8. Both theorems are complete proofs: they compile with no sorry, and #print axioms reports only {propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice} (the two main theorems depend on exactly those three). The positive side is an induction machine on explicit vertex lists (closed tours for even n >= 8 from four explicit base lists at n = 8,10,12,14 plus an 8-column insertion step; open tours for odd n >= 9 from two bases at n = 9,11 plus a 4-column step; the small cases n = 1,4,5 by explicit witnesses checked with decide). The negative side is degree and bipartite-parity arguments for the small cases plus, for the two hard zero values n = 6,7, a cut-barrier lemma (deleting a vertex list S that leaves more than |S|+1 labelled blocks blocks any Hamiltonian path) applied to explicit certificates decided by the kernel. The case n = 1 on the open side is a pre-freeze correction (F0b) recorded in the task card. Novelty adjudication, copied from the pipeline's four-round exclusivity review included here in full with every zero-hit query (lineage reconnaissance over literature / OEIS / formalisation ecosystems; a narrow-path deep dive; a feasibility report that resolved three blockers and identified the existence characterisation as the provable core; and a full-text fourth round): no occupying record found for the existence characterisation of open or closed tours on two-square 3 x n boards. The nearest published neighbours are delimited explicitly - Miller-Farnsworth 2013 (3 x n, one square removed, closed tours), Srichote et al. 2022 (4 x n, two squares removed, closed tours), Bi et al. 2015 (the 4 x n two-square question), DeMaio-Hippchen 2009 (minimal removal count), Schwenk 1991 (full boards) - and none of them treats two-square 3 x n boards or open-tour existence on deficient 3 x n boards. The counting companion of the same family (the number of open/closed tours) is auxiliary computational data of the source task, is not claimed and not submitted to OEIS (the historical OEIS sequence queries of the novelty record, all zero-hit, are included in the record verbatim), and is not part of this note. Claim note under CC-BY-4.0, code under MIT. Produced by the AI4Math pipeline (LLM generation + Lean kernel adjudication; task budgets copied verbatim from the task ledger: 29 of 36 permitted agent-run samples, 4 of 6 llm-calls (one node smoke plus three roundtrip attempts that failed at the transport layer, after which the semantic roundtrip was re-routed through the agent channel), 49 of 56 strict kernel compiles plus separately-ledgered compile-debug probes; this note consumed 0 pipeline LLM calls against a cap of 4). The narrative paper of this result is prepared separately under the pipeline's paper lane and will reference this DOI.
